settings.subtitle: The clinical baseline. The formula most appointments call for.
settings.trust_line: UK formulated · Cosmetic product · CPSR assessed

settings.headline: Clinical is the standard. Two more strengths sit above it.
settings.body: Most clients choose Clinical; some go straight to Advanced — a higher-strength cream for longer or more sensitive work. Professional is the highest strength, developed with practitioners and available without restriction.

settings.title: Start with clean, dry skin.
settings.body: Remove any make-up, oil or moisturiser over the area so nothing sits between the product and the skin.

settings.title: Apply a thick, visible layer.
settings.body: Let it sit on the surface rather than rubbing it in. Customers who get the best results typically report applying a generous layer — thick enough to look visibly white on the skin — rather than a thin one.

settings.title: Leave it in place.
settings.body: Follow your practitioner's guidance for the procedure you've booked.

settings.title: Remove before your appointment.
settings.body: Wipe away with a clean cloth or tissue, or as your practitioner directs.

settings.headline: A short routine ahead of your appointment.
settings.closer: Your practitioner is the best guide for timing specific to your booking. The steps above are the standard preparation routine.

settings.label: Strength
settings.value: Clinical — the baseline in the Senseless system. Cream format.

settings.question: Is Clinical the right strength for my appointment?
settings.answer: For most, yes. For longer or more sensitive work, Advanced is the higher strength.

settings.question: What size should I choose?
settings.answer: 10g suits a single appointment; 30g suits a regular regimen.

settings.question: What's in it?
settings.answer: A UK-formulated cosmetic preparation. The full ingredients list is on the packaging.

settings.question: How long does it last?
settings.answer: Senseless is designed for use ahead of a specific appointment. Duration varies by client and by application — your practitioner is the best guide.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
